section: 11. ODESSA and the Neo-Nazi Thule Society
description: An informant reveals the connection between the Frankfurt neo-Nazi organization Thule Tradition Society and the ODESSA Nazi remnants, the museum exhibition protest incident, and the deep concealment of old Nazis.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew looked at Ms. Gray in surprise, almost standing up, but he suppressed the impulse and sat back down.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "3200 marks twice!"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Quickly go to pay, then approach to observe that thing.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The staff nearby signal for you to follow them to the small room behind the auction hall to complete the transaction.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: 3600 marks! Andrew sighed inwardly; this little trinket looked like it could only serve as a decorative piece on a plate. He was willing to pay at most 50 dollars for it.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Cash only, ma'am."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Take out the money and pay.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: That's 3200 marks, saving 400 marks to enjoy a few more good meals.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: @player4 At first glance, it is covered with geometric patterns composed of lines and dots, resembling abstract circuit diagrams; but upon closer observation, you can see that the dots are snake heads with flickering tongues, and the lines are snake bodies, together forming a double-headed serpent motif.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Let me see, you're quite skilled in many things.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Can I have a bag to carry it? It's a bit awkward to hold."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew waits to participate in the auction of Lehmann's remaining items. He wonders if there might be some "hidden layers" among his belongings.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Of course, but I'm sorry, you'll need to pack it yourself. We are not responsible for the lot after it's sold."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Put the cube inside.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The moment you touch it with your hand, within the circuit diagram formed by the double-headed serpents, one snake suddenly comes to life, twisting and slithering to the center of the top of the box.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player4>'s Sanity Check:

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Then that snake winks at you and flicks its tongue. The tongue leaves the mouth, turning into several curved lines, which finally twist and turn, piecing together into this line of text: "Now go outside and buy a bouquet of roses."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Unable to believe your eyes, your hand trembles slightly, trying hard to stay steady and not drop it.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Meanwhile, your perception of your surroundings is becoming sharper, just like what you experienced at Lehmann's house. You can feel the discomfort of the information torrent impacting your brain, and that sense of omniscient exhilaration...

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Is there a flower shop nearby?

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew sits in his seat waiting for the auction to continue, but sees Gray leaving the small room and heading out, so he also stands up and follows her.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You see the heated debates in other exhibition halls, Andrew waiting outside, a large crowd gathered around Auction Hall No. 1, and a little girl selling flowers with a basket by the roadside outside the Judicial Auction Bureau.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Hiss" Alison taps her forehead, quickly walks out of the venue, signals Andrew to follow, and heads towards the little girl selling flowers.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew just follows along, having no idea what's happening, but once outside the main door, he quickens his pace to catch up with Ms. Gray.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: When you see this scene, the intense discomfort you just felt suddenly disappears; doors and walls once again block your vision.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "We spent 3200 on this thing? Isn't it just a decorative piece?" Andrew is somewhat anxious. "But since it's spent, it's spent. I don't think we have much chance of taking this money back anyway."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "The longer the night, the more dreams; I'm worried other organizations might also be eyeing this thing. We have too little information; if we don't solve the problem, we won't be alive to spend it. Moreover, this thing is strange; I'm experiencing the same situation I felt at Lehmann's house again."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I'm sorry, ma'am! There's a crowd gathered outside now; they insist on the item just auctioned, saying the price can be negotiated."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew lowers his head, secretly looking for the location of the back door, but the car is still at the front!

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I'm sorry, please tell them I have no intention of reselling, and I hope they won't obtain any information about me."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew also tried to check his pockets, but there was nothing like that inside.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Naturally, we are a legitimate judicial auction and certainly not afraid of these gangsters. We can take you out through the side door, but you'd better be careful and stay away from these guys."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Thank you so much. You mentioned gangsters just now? Are they members of some notorious gang?" He asked the staff while following them out through the side door.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew followed Gray closely, "I'm with her, I'm one of the good guys."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Considering the big business you brought today and the fact that you bought something no one else wanted, he kindly reminded you, "I've heard some rumors. I think they might be peripheral members of the 'Free Corps.' This organization has been quite active lately, but they haven't caused any major trouble yet."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Thank you very much, I'll be careful." Keep an eye out to see if anyone is following us, and quickly head over to the little girl selling flowers.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player2> wants to discuss something with me privately? Well done, I won't tell anyone the content.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The large, noisy group of people are still harassing the bailiffs and staff, demanding to enter Auction Hall No. 1. No one noticed you slipping away quietly.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Where are we going? Why are we heading towards the front door?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I don't know why, but I saw a sentence appear on that cube, telling me to buy a rose. There's a little girl selling flowers at the front door. Let's give it a try."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Alright, but the front door isn't very peaceful right now. I'll cover the rear for you." "Or we could get in the car first and call the little girl over from there."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You arrived in front of the little girl. Only one bouquet remained in her flower basket, seemingly prepared just for you.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Little sister, I'll take this bouquet. Go home early, how much is it?" Alison took off her mask and showed a friendly smile.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew remained completely unaware of everything.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "One Mark!" The little girl thanked you happily, handed you the flowers, and then walked straight away.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Examine the flowers, is there anything special about them?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Then, you noticed a strange change: across the street, originally a café was right next to a barbershop; but after you bought the rose, you discovered a new shop had appeared between the café and the barbershop, as if it had grown out of the ground, "squeezing" the other two shops to the sides.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew looked troubled.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Is that an illusion?" Alison pinched her own arm.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The shop Andrew saw had a weathered wooden sign at the door, engraved with "MacTavish House," and below it, written in Gaelic: "Tobar nan Seann Rudan" (meaning "Well of Ancient Things"). The heavy oak door had a small glass window embedded in it, through which a dim yellow light and a wooden bar could be faintly seen. The shop's exterior walls were mottled with a damp, muddy gray hue. A faded tartan cloth hung from an iron ring by the door, exactly the kind of decoration you saw in your grandfather's pub during your childhood.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Andrew, do you see that?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "I see it, but I'm not sure." Andrew looked around, checking the flow of people and traffic. "Shall we go check it out?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Let's go in and take a look. At this point, nothing would surprise me anymore." Alison walked towards the magical shop and pushed the door open.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Regardless, the appearance of this shop was completely different from the surrounding German stores. However, the pedestrians on the street hurried along, showing no reaction to this oddly styled shop, as if they couldn't see it.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew first touches that area, feels the boundary with the surrounding shops, and observes pedestrians' reactions to this place. Go in! Andrew follows closely.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You arrived at the door and could see a sign hanging that said "Open"; looking up, you could see the large signboard with the shop name written in your language (Irish and Highland Gaelic): if translated directly, it would be "The First People."

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player4>'s Sanity Check:

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew held on! Although his head felt dizzy and his whole body was filled with discomfort, he still maintained a clear mind and proceeded along the intended path.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You feel that Andrew is your newly born, never-before-met, dearest little brother. Time is so magical; though it was only a second, it feels as if you've missed him for decades.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Oh, Andrew! It's so good to see you're alright!" Alison affectionately hugged Andrew's head.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Although the flow of time here seems incredibly strange, the interior decor of the shop is unexpectedly "normal." The front shelves hold daily necessities like makeup mirrors and combs, along with some silver jars emitting smoky bubbles, which seem to contain scented incense. The shelves on both sides display various small dolls made of porcelain, metal, and cloth.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "What's wrong, sis, what happened to you?" Andrew retreats fearfully, keeping his distance. "Thanks to you, I'm not dead yet."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: @player4 The footsteps from behind the shelves are light and unhurried, and then a woman in an apron emerges. She has smooth chestnut hair, a few strands slightly curled, carrying the scent of Oxfordshire's rainy air. Her eyes are a warm hazel, and the corners of her mouth hold a perfectly measured smile, as if she were the owner of a bookstore in the old town or the kindly lady from the village grocery who always slipped you an extra piece of toffee as a child. Her attire is understated but neat, and her apron carries a faint scent of roses, reminiscent of dried flowers commonly found in old English country houses. Her voice is soft yet exudes a familiar warmth: "Hello, madam, what can I get for you today?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Hello, may I ask what this place is..."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: She wipes her hands on her apron and walks over. The distance is about five or six meters, and she takes a few seconds, but in your perception, those few seconds seem compressed into an instant and then stretched into infinity—although your brain is certain she walked over at a normal speed, you can't be sure how long it actually took.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: A red-haired lass, not uncommon but not rare in the Lowlands of Scotland, Andrew scratches his dyed brown-blond hair.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "This is The First Man. I am Hestria."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "How did this shop grow out of the wall? It's truly magical. And the moment I stepped inside, I felt terribly uncomfortable all over. I only started feeling better after adjusting."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Taking out the cube: "I was guided here by this thing. It's been a truly magical experience... Could you please tell us about this place and what this thing in my hand is?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "The First Man Trading Company. The reason we've invited you here this time is mainly to confirm the status of this 'artifact.' If nothing unexpected happened, it should currently be in Dr. Heim's possession, but clearly, something went wrong."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Who is Heim?" Andrew forgets instantly.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Storing spells? Although it sounds incredible, I've experienced too many incredible things these past few days." Alison tries touching the cube again.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Would you like to try it? Let me show you."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Is... is this something we're allowed to see?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "You might as well touch this little point of light."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Extends a finger to try touching it.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "The moment you entered, I already knew how you obtained this device. Since you acquired it through legal means and in good faith, I will regard you as the current owners of the MK2. I must teach you how to use our product to avoid any accidents."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "That would be a great help. We're completely clueless about this thing."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The moment Gray touches it, countless strange whispers echo in his mind. Information floods in, causing severe information overload.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player4>'s Sanity Check:

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You gradually understand everything: This is a device that compresses and stores "spells." The spell stored within no longer requires preparation time, space, magic circles, or similar conditions; it can be used instantly. To invoke the spell inside, throw it toward a mirror. Another advantage is that it has a fully automatic "foolproof" operating system built-in. Any ordinary person, without needing to know all the incantations or principles of the spell, can invoke it by using the mirror as a medium, summoning and clicking on this blue point of light, and silently thinking of the target.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison holds her head. "This is... the spell I can cast using this device?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Hestria takes a cloth doll from the shelf. It begins writhing frantically like a frightened little white mouse. Although its button-made features can't show any expression, you inexplicably sense its emotions—the profound fear and despair from the depths of its being. "Allow me to introduce you to the first use of the Goloi Blessing Spell here: taking the souls of those who owe debts to this shop, putting them into dolls, and selling them to repay the debts."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew feels a chill. "In what manner are they repaid?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Generally speaking, the souls are used for experiments, all sorts of..."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Can I take a look at what a human soul looks like? Like a thick stew... and delicious? Just one look, okay?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Does releasing the spell inside have any effect on the user?" Alison shifts her gaze away from the doll.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "No, any ordinary person can use it."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Truly magical... What about the number of uses?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: @player6 "You really are a crazy one. That metaphor has given me some unnecessary doubts about tonight's stew."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Using this method to put an old man's soul into a young person's body... wouldn't that grant immortality?" Alison had a sudden flash of insight, recalling information she had seen before. "So the old man in Solomon's House actually has the soul of an old Nazi inside him!"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Of course, if you simply want to 'take a look,' you first need to define the meaning of 'look.' Because in my limited experience, those who want to 'see' a soul usually end up wanting to take a bite."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "You have a chef here too? That's great, I'm also a chef."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison hugs Andrew's head and ruffles his hair. "Calm down, Andrew. Don't touch unknown things recklessly. Let your sister take a look first."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: She brings a small doll close to your eyes. Through its dark button eyes, you see... its "soul" is like a water-soaked cotton wad—damp, heavy, and exuding an indescribable sense of brokenness. The texture of the soul isn't pure and transparent as depicted in religious texts; it's viscous, constantly twisting and deforming, like spiritual residue forcibly torn out by some power. For a moment, your vision is flooded with distorted images—smooth yet fragmented ripples, like melting wax on water, dripping, spreading, vanishing... only to coalesce again the next moment, trying to piece itself back into some complete form.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "This completely kills my appetite..." Andrew shrinks back in fear.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: @player4 "Generally, there's no limit, but it's best not to exceed a hundred times in one day."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison releases Andrew, hesitates for a moment, and looks around at the various items on the shelves. "You said this is a shop. Can we also buy things we need here? Our current situation isn't good. I want to seize every opportunity we can use."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Sorry, we only accept barter. You don't have any spells or magical items that interest the Trading House."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Alright... Are the dolls used to store souls specially made, or can any container work? I mean, maybe I can use this spell to obtain some souls for payment..." Alison stares at the box.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew should have felt fear, but he's afraid that if he shows fear, he might never get the chance to feel fear again.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "No, I think you misunderstood. This isn't some gathering of black mages using souls as equivalent currency. I reiterate, we only accept barter with spells or magical items."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Alright, thank you very much for teaching us how to use this device. Perhaps we can find similar things from those who tried to steal it, if we're still alive by then. How can we return here to trade with you?" Alison is somewhat disappointed, but learning this spell is already a significant gain.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "That depends on the value of the items to us. When the Trading House deems it necessary, the door will open for you anytime, anywhere."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Is there any way to identify or deal with someone who has used this spell to transfer their soul? One of our superiors might no longer be himself."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "I wonder if we can save those innocents who were replaced..."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "There's also a retrospection incantation that pairs with the Blessing spell, recorded in the Old World Black Book. Recite it in front of the body that has had its soul transferred, and a black mark will appear on its face."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "So, at that time, many souls would be in one body?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "The Blessing spell can completely transfer one person's soul into another person's body, but it cannot destroy the original soul of that person. You might have misunderstood."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Oh? In that case, which of the two souls controls the body? Would it be like having a split personality?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Correct, it generally manifests as symptoms of split personality."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "If one soul achieves a great victory in the fight, does it truly take over the body?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "There's also this trick?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Not exactly. Completely destroying a person's soul is extremely difficult. Dr. Joseph Heim conducted numerous experiments to destroy souls, but all ended in failure."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Where can we find that book? Or do you have that incantation here?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "The Trading House hasn't acquired it because it has no use for it."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "It seems our good luck ends here, but it's still a significant gain. Thank you, Miss Hestria." Alison bows respectfully.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Alright, thank you!"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Take care~"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "By the way, I saw someone say that traveling through time might attract pursuit by some kind of 'Tengu.' Just now, when I arrived here, I felt like I didn't know how much time had passed... Will we encounter such a situation?" Alison suddenly thinks of this.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Hah~ This isn't time travel. You'll understand once you step outside and check your watch."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I understand. I look forward to meeting you again."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The moment you push the shop door open and step out, you still experience a disorientation in your sense of time. However, with your previous experience, you don't make a fuss this time.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Andrew, was I just dreaming?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "I don't believe you were dreaming just now. It all seemed very real."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We've really been dragged into a huge mess... What's next, vampires, werewolves, aliens?" The successive mental shocks make Alison vent with self-abandonment.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Yes, you're right!"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Meanwhile, after a frantic drive and adding 50 Marks worth of fuel, David and player5 finally enter Aschaffenburg.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "God, feels like we've come to quite a place." David whispers to Rabin.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "This place looks full of decay." Tucking the gun at the waist, putting on Lehmann's bracelet, hands on hips, sizing up this bar.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David looks around to see if anyone is secretly watching us?

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: First, walk around the outside, see how many entrances/exits this place has, assess the optimal escape route.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: The cycle of fate is like shackles, and are you about to gamble on the untraceable one at this moment?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: @player5 On the surface, there's only the main door as an entrance/exit.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: @player3 Also check how many lookouts are around while you're at it.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player5>'s Spot Hidden check result:

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Yes, but obviously they are hiding very skillfully."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Let's go. Even if it's a dragon's den or a tiger's lair, we have to venture in."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David, who also found nothing, agrees.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Pushing the door open and entering, you find the interior space is actually quite large, even with a small empty stage. One can imagine how lively it was in its heyday. But now, although there are many customers, they are shabbily dressed and only focused on drinking gloomily. The whole atmosphere is dull, as if only the stereo playing The Beatles is the only living thing.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Look around, especially observing the customers. Following the techniques learned as agents, find a corner seat and sit down.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The bartender behind the counter wipes a glass with a clean white cloth. His gaze lingers on you for a moment, then he reveals a somewhat playful smile. His face is thin, deep nasolabial folds making him appear older than his actual age, and those eyes with a cunning glint make it hard to fathom what he's really thinking.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Push the door open and enter, rather casually scanning the surroundings to see if there are any noteworthy individuals, then sizing up the bartender and the types of liquor on the shelves, before casually sitting down at the bar.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Soda water." David says. He thinks at least one of the two shouldn't drink alcohol.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Come here just for a sip of soda water? You're really something." Despite saying that, he skillfully pushes a glass over, takes a bottle of soda water from the cabinet, and pours it for you.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "I once heard that experienced bartenders can roughly judge a new customer's preferences at first glance. I've always hoped to have the chance to meet such a skilled bartender." Leaning on the bar, propping up the side of the face with the hand wearing Lehmann's bracelet, looking at the bartender with a slight smile.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The bartender raises an eyebrow slightly, the smile at the corner of his mouth deepening. "Oh? It seems you're someone who knows the trade." He narrows his eyes slightly, fingertips gently turning an empty glass, saying in a low voice: "Let me see... You're not the type who goes for fancy cocktails. Too sweet or too complex flavors would bore you. You prefer drinks with a clean, crisp taste, yet with a hint of depth." He pauses, then slowly says: "I guess you'd like a 'Manhattan'—classic, restrained, but with a long aftertaste. Also, suitable for mourning the dead."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David listens silently to the conversation between the bartender and Rabin. It seems the people at Hermes already know Lehmann is dead. So what is his attitude towards us? David narrows his eyes, trying to discern a clue from the bartender's expression.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player3>'s Psychology check result:

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You can see the bartender's expression is very natural, not deliberately hiding anything—seven parts curiosity, three parts wariness. And when mentioning Lehmann, he's as indifferent as if mentioning a stray dog on the roadside.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Precise analysis. Pleased to meet an excellent bartender here." Glancing at the prices on the drink menu, he pays readily. "However, compared to mourning friends, I prefer attending rivals' funerals and making some new friends."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Let's be open. I don't care where you got Lehman's bracelet, and that person is insignificant. But you seem to be here for this?" He mixes you a Manhattan.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "There was a van accident in the outskirts yesterday, a few people died." Taking a sip of the drink, he speaks slowly, observing the bartender's reaction closely. "We don't get along with those people. Perhaps we have room for cooperation."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The bartender gently shakes the cocktail shaker in his hand, slowly pouring out a glass of amber liquid, his movements as steady as ever. However, upon hearing the words "van accident," his wrist movement imperceptibly hitches for a moment before returning to normal as he slides the glass towards you.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David crosses his legs, watching to see how Rabin drinks his soup next.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "We don't need a goods trade for now. What we need is information." He shakes his head after speaking, takes another sip of the drink, and savors it carefully. "In return, we can also provide some of the information we possess."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Of course, my brain isn't completely numbed by alcohol yet. I can offer a free consultation and explore the possibility of our cooperation."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "I'm all ears."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The boss puts down the glass and rag in his hands, takes out a revolver and a single bullet from under the bar. He reaches out, casually spins the cylinder with a crisp click, then slides the gun in front of the investigator, lightly slapping the bar with his palm: "Load this one bullet, spin it randomly, then we take turns shooting at our own knees. If you get shot in the end, you leave immediately. If I get shot in the end, I'll accept any deal you propose."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David wants to listen to the bartender's accent. He is fluent in many languages and is very curious about which side the Hermes leader is from.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Let me see, you're quite skilled in many things.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Interesting, I like it." Takes the gun and immediately pulls the trigger once, aiming at his own knee.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player5>'s Handgun check result:

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Click..." This shot is a dud.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Good courage!" Takes the gun without hesitation.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Lady Luck favors you once again. Dud.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David blends into the crowd of patrons and places a bet on the boss winning. That way, even if player5 gets shot, he can earn some prosthetic money. Bets on Rabin getting shot.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Hahaha, interesting, interesting." Downs the "Manhattan" in one gulp, takes the gun, and pulls the trigger without hesitation.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: player5's final chance. Dud!

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Places the gun on the bar. "No need to fire this shot."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The bar erupts in cheers and boos. Gamblers excitedly or disappointedly slap tables and exchange chips. The air is thick with the smell of alcohol and tobacco. Servers quickly step forward to tally the winnings from the gamble, while the bartender puts away the firearm. "Not bad. Lady Luck was on your side." He speaks leisurely, his gaze lingering on you for a moment. "You not only have guts but also made me some money."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Good, then I'll ask directly." Shifts to a more comfortable position. "What do you know about the House of Solomon, Heim, and Adolf Müller?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Hmm? I thought you'd ask about the Free Corps." His brow furrows.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "The Free Corps is our common enemy. We also have some intelligence on them. We can exchange that information later."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Or which intelligence agencies are in the city. What you're asking is indeed a bit unexpected."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Intelligence values quality over quantity. If you can't provide valuable information on this aspect, I doubt other parties can provide the intelligence we're looking for either."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "The problem is, the things you're asking about typically don't appear on any of our regular clients' lists. It's like going to great lengths just to ask your neighbor what filling yesterday's pie had."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: A look of disappointment can't help but appear on his face. "So it seems you also don't know what's really behind the Free Corps."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I do know a bit about that, actually."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Yes, Adolf Müller. We are aware of this habit you mentioned." Nods slightly.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: He leaned forward slightly, hands clasped, not surprised by your questions. "As for the client's identity, I can't tell you directly. Rules are rules. However..."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "This is already sufficient." Looking at the newspaper with a knowing smile. "Then, regarding the 'Hunt' operation executed by the Academy's 'Kant' in December 1960, do you have any related intelligence?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "In 1960, they sent a guy named 'Kant' to Argentina to eliminate 'an enemy of their people'. For this, they approached 'Hermes' to buy some special weapons and fake documents."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "So that's how it is, I roughly understand." Scattered clues gradually connected, producing a vague sense of clarity. "Let me sort this out first."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "My friend had some unpleasantness with some people wearing peaked caps earlier on the day of the car accident. To prevent misunderstandings, I'd like to know, what is the connection between Andrius Rilke and the Free Corps?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: He angrily stubbed his cigarette out on the table. "That bastard Rilke has suddenly become enlightened over the past six months, as if someone in the underworld is helping him. He's been relentlessly targeting Hermes' transaction points and secret warehouses, causing our business to decline steadily, forcing us to leave Frankfurt."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "In the communications between 'The Troupe' and 'The Pawnshop', they mentioned 'the London representative in Frankfurt'. What does this represent?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: @player2 "This isn't normal. According to our clues, Rilke and the Free Corps absolutely have some kind of connection. We suspect their backing might be some neo-Nazi organization."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "We both know this, but aren't they currently in internal turmoil? They shouldn't be able to accomplish much for the time being."
